mainTopic: When witnesses are liable for שבועת העדות: testimony about a קנס, the משנה's exemption for non-money cases, and the sources that this oath applies only to money claims.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that makes witnesses liable for שבועת העדות when they deny knowing that a man slandered a girl. That case is a קנס, and admitting to a קנס normally exempts a person. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: admitting exempts only when there are no witnesses at all. Next comes a new משנה. It rules that witnesses are exempt when the oath concerns lineage, such as being a כהן or a לוי, or concerns crimes that carry the death penalty, because no money is at stake. The גמרא then asks how a person can make witnesses swear about money owed to someone else. שמואל answers that he holds a הרשאה, and the גמרא shows that a הרשאה can be written for movables as long as the defendant has not yet denied the claim. Finally, a ברייתא brings several sources that שבועת העדות applies only to money claims. רבי אליעזר learns it from the repeated ״או״ and defends the comparison against רוצח and סוטה. רבי עקיבא learns it from the word ״מאלה״, רבי יוסי הגלילי from 'he saw or he knew', and רבי שמעון from a comparison to פקדון. רבי שמעון also begins a קל וחומר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא about witnesses to slander
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: witnesses who deny testimony that someone slandered a girl are liable for שבועת העדות, but if the man admitted on his own, he is exempt from the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A father said to witnesses: Come testify for me] that so-and-so slandered my daughter. The witnesses are liable. If he admitted on his own, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא it is using as a challenge. The ברייתא makes witnesses liable for denying testimony about a case that is really a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment of a מוציא שם רע is a קנס, and the ברייתא itself says that admitting exempts him. If his own admission can wipe out the payment, it is hard to see how the witnesses' testimony is what makes him pay. Yet the ברייתא still makes the witnesses liable for שבועת העדות, and that is the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who falsely claims his new bride was unfaithful during betrothal; he pays a fixed fine
A fixed penalty payment set by the תורה, not based on actual damage
They are liable (here, the witnesses, for a false oath of testimony)
He admitted on his own, with his own mouth
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people here. 'חייבין' (plural) refers to the witnesses who swore falsely. 'פטור' (singular) refers to the slanderer who admitted.

phrases.english: that so-and-so put out
phrases.notes: These are the father's words to the witnesses, continuing a ברייתא that started before this section.

phrases.english: a bad name about my daughter – they are liable.
If he admitted on his own – he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהוֹצִיא אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי שֵׁם רַע עַל בִּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that was started before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שבועת העדות does not apply to testimony about a קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מוציא שם רע case is a קנס, yet the ברייתא makes witnesses liable for denying testimony about it.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says witnesses come and testify even after the man admits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says: Let witnesses come and testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows one specific תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, admitting does not stop the witnesses, so their testimony can still make him pay the fine. That means their denial really does cost the father money, and so they are liable for שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Let witnesses come and testify, even after an admission

phrases.english: Whose is this?
It is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who says: Let witnesses come and testify.
phrases.notes: He means that even after the man admits, the witnesses can still testify and make him pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Admitting to a קנס always cancels it, so testimony about it never truly causes payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, witnesses still testify after an admission, so their testimony does cause payment.

steps.title: The last clause seems to follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא's last clause says one who admits is exempt, which sounds like the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: If he admitted on his own, he is exempt. Now we have come to the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave by pointing to the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that admitting to a קנס exempts a person. The ending of the ברייתא, 'admitted, exempt,' seems to say exactly that. Then the beginning would follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the end would follow the רבנן, which is very awkward.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the last clause
We have come to the view of the Rabbis
One who admits to a fine is exempt (the view of the רבנן)

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
If he admitted on his own – he is exempt,
we have come to the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause exempts one who admits, which matches the רבנן, so the ברייתא would be split between two opinions.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The whole ברייתא is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Admitting exempts only when there are no witnesses at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole thing is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and this is what it means: You only find the exemption for admitting on his own where there are no witnesses at all and he admitted on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the last clause in a narrower way, so the whole ברייתא fits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון agrees that admitting exempts from a קנס. He only disagrees when witnesses exist. So the last clause is about a case with no witnesses, and it does not contradict the first clause, where witnesses exist.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole ברייתא
And this is what it is saying
You do not find it, except...
There are no witnesses at all

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, admitting to a קנס exempts only when there are no witnesses. When witnesses exist, they can still testify and make him pay, so witnesses who falsely deny that testimony are liable for שבועת העדות.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא,
phrases.english: All of it is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
and this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ הוֹדָה מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: you do not find a case of admitting on his own
where he is exempt,
except where there are no witnesses at all
and he admitted on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the last clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last clause means admitting exempts even when there are witnesses, which is the view of the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last clause is about a case with no witnesses at all, which רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון also agrees exempts him.

steps.title: New משנה: oaths about family status
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a list of cases where someone makes witnesses swear to testify about lineage: being a כהן or a לוי, or not being a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'I make you swear: if you do not come and testify that I am a כהן, that I am a לוי, that I am not the son of a divorced woman, that I am not the son of a חלוצה, that so-and-so is a כהן, that so-and-so is a לוי, that he is not the son of a divorced woman, that he is not the son of a חלוצה...'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It lists oaths about family status. This step is the first half of the list, and the ruling comes at the end of the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case here is about lineage, and none of them is about money. That is the key to the ruling that follows, because שבועת העדות applies only to testimony about money.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear: the standard wording for making witnesses take an oath
The son of a כהן and a divorced woman. He is a חלל and is not fit for כהונה
The son of a כהן and a woman who went through חליצה
So-and-so: an unnamed person

phrases.english: MISHNA:
'I make you swear,
if you do not come and testify
that I am a priest, that I am a Levite,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינִי בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה, שֶׁאֵינִי בֶּן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: that I am not the son of a divorced woman, that I am not the son of a חלוצה,
phrases.notes: He means the son of a כהן who married one of these women. Such a son loses his כהונה status.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי כֹּהֵן, שֶׁאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי לֵוִי,
phrases.english: that so-and-so is a priest, that so-and-so is a Levite,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: that he is not the son of a divorced woman, that he is not the son of a חלוצה,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁבִּיעַ אֲנִי עֲלֵיכֶם, אִם לֹא תָבוֹאוּ וְתָעִידוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון discussion in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This step lists the lineage cases. The ruling (exempt) comes in the next step.

steps.title: Death-penalty cases, and the ruling: exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds cases of crimes that carry the death penalty: rape or seduction of one's own daughter, a son injuring his father, and injury or burning on שבת. It then rules that in all the listed cases the witnesses are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...that so-and-so raped his daughter, or seduced his daughter, or that my son injured me, or that my friend injured me, or that he set my grain stack on fire on שבת': these witnesses are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list and gives the ruling: the witnesses are exempt from שבועת העדות in every one of these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crime cases look like they involve payment. But each crime carries the death penalty, so no money will be paid (קים ליה בדרבה מיניה). Since no money is at stake in any case on the list, the oath is not a monetary שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Raped
Seduced
Injured or wounded
A stack of grain
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume these crime cases are exempt because no damage was done. Damage was done. The reason is that each act carries the death penalty, so the money payment falls away.

phrases.english: that so-and-so raped his own daughter,
or seduced his own daughter,
or that my son injured me,
or that my friend injured me,
phrases.notes: The words 'on שבת' at the end of the list apply here too.

phrases.english: that he set my grain stack on fire on Shabbat'
– these are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list begun in step 5 and gives the ruling for all the cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who refuse testimony that would not produce a money payment are exempt from שבועת העדות.
steps.whatToRemember: שבועת העדות applies only when the testimony would win someone money. Cases about lineage, and cases where the death penalty cancels the payment, are exempt.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה clashes with the later clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that an oath about money owed to someone else (מנה לפלוני ביד פלוני) would make the witnesses liable. But a later clause says they are liable only if they hear the demand from the plaintiff himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason they are exempt is that he said 'so-and-so is a כהן' or 'so-and-so is a לוי'. That implies that if he said 'so-and-so has a מנה in the hands of so-and-so', they would be liable. But the later clause teaches: not until they hear it from the mouth of the plaintiff!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads an implied rule out of the משנה. It then shows that this rule seems to contradict another part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה picked the example 'so-and-so is a כהן', about someone else. That implies the only problem is that no money is involved. So 'so-and-so is owed money' should make the witnesses liable, even though the speaker is not the person owed the money. Yet the later clause (on 35a) requires the demand to come from the plaintiff himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... This opens an inference from the wording
A sum of one hundred זוז
The later clause of the משנה
The plaintiff, the one making the claim

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that it was 'so-and-so is a priest,'
'so-and-so is a Levite';
but if 'so-and-so has a מנה in the hands of so-and-so' – they would be liable;
But the later clause teaches:
not until they hear it from the mouth of the plaintiff!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads an inference out of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that a third party can make witnesses liable by having them swear about someone else's money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later clause requires the oath to come from the plaintiff himself. Here the speaker is not the plaintiff, so the witnesses should not be liable.

steps.title: שמואל: the speaker has power of attorney
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the money case works when the speaker comes with a הרשאה, a document authorizing him to act for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it is where he comes with a power of attorney.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the contradiction. The person giving the oath is the owner's authorized agent, so he counts as the plaintiff.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person with a הרשאה stands in for the owner. So when he says 'so-and-so has a מנה with so-and-so', the demand is treated as coming from the plaintiff, and the later clause is satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: Power of attorney: authorization to claim on someone else's behalf

phrases.english: שמואל said:
It is where he comes with a power of attorney.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the speaker is an authorized agent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The speaker is a stranger with no connection to the claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: The speaker holds a הרשאה, so he counts as the plaintiff.

steps.title: נהרדעי: no power of attorney for movables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the sages of נהרדעא said we do not write an authorization document (אורכתא) for movable property, and a מנה is movable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the sages of נהרדעא said: we do not write a power of attorney for movable property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer. A loan of money is movable property, and נהרדעי say no הרשאה is written for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no הרשאה can be written for movables, then שמואל's agent could not exist in a case about a מנה. That would bring back the original contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of the city of נהרדעא
An authorization document (הרשאה)
Movable property

phrases.english: But didn't the sages of Neharde'a say:
We do not write an authorization document for movable property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's case of an agent with a הרשאה for a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נהרדעי rule that no הרשאה is written for movables, so the agent in שמואל's case could not exist.

steps.title: The rule applies only after the defendant denied the claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: נהרדעי's rule applies only where the defendant has already denied the claim. If he has not denied it, we do write a הרשאה, even for movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies where he denied it. But where he did not deny it, we do write one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits נהרדעי's rule so that שמואל's answer can stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the defendant has denied the claim, the owner holds only a disputed claim, and that cannot be handed over by a הרשאה. Before any denial, the money is still clearly the owner's, so an agent can be authorized. That is the case in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only... (limits a rule to a certain case)
He denied it (the defendant denied the claim)
We write (the document)

steps.whatToRemember: A third party can make witnesses liable for שבועת העדות about money only with a הרשאה. A הרשאה for movables can be written as long as the defendant has not yet denied the claim.

phrases.english: This applies only where he denied it,
but where he did not deny it – we write one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by limiting נהרדעי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No הרשאה is ever written for movables.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only after the defendant has denied the claim. Before that, a הרשאה is written, so שמואל's answer stands.

steps.title: Where do we learn that this oath is only about money?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks for the source that the פסוק of שבועת העדות deals only with monetary claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we know that the verse is only talking about a claim for money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a ברייתא that asks a question. This sets up the next step, where רבי אליעזר gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said witnesses are exempt in death-penalty cases and are liable only when money is claimed. The ברייתא now asks where the תורה itself limits שבועת העדות to money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? A request for a source
The verse
A monetary claim, a demand for money

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that the verse is speaking
phrases.notes: "The verse" here is the פסוק about witnesses who swear they know nothing, ויקרא 5:1.

phrases.english: only about a monetary claim?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בִּתְבִיעַת מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the הרשאה issue, the גמרא turns to the scriptural source for the משנה's rule that only money claims count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that שבועת העדות is limited to monetary claims.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns it from the repeated word "or"
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר makes a גזירה שוה: the ״או״ words of שבועת העדות are compared to the ״או״ words of שבועת הפקדון, which deals only with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: The word "or" appears several times here, and the word "or" appears several times there. Just as there the verse is talking only about money claims, so too here it is talking only about money claims.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question. Both oath passages use the word "or" again and again, so he says they share the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath about a deposit (שבועת הפקדון) is clearly about money: deposits, loans, robbery and lost items. Because both passages share the repeated ״או״, רבי אליעזר moves the "money only" limit over to שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of ״או״: the repeated word "or"
"Here" and "there": the two passages being compared
Learning one passage from another because they share the same word
An oath denying that one holds someone's deposit or money

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Several "or"s are stated here,
and several "or"s are stated there;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21–22. This is the oath about a deposit.

phrases.english: just as there it is speaking
only about a monetary claim,
so too here it is speaking
only about a monetary claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״אוֹאִין״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״אוֹאִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the repeated ״או״ in שבועת הפקדון, which deals only with money.

steps.title: Challenge from the "or"s about a murderer
steps.stepSummary: The parsha of the רוצח also repeats ״או״, yet it is not about money. So the repeated word should not prove a money limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the "or"s written about a murderer prove the opposite! They are also "or"s, and they are not talking about money claims.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אליעזר's comparison. It points to another passage with repeated "or" that has nothing to do with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word ״או״ alone made a passage about money, the murderer passage would be about money too, and it is not. So the shared word looks too weak to carry the "money only" limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A murderer
"Let them prove": a counter-example that breaks a comparison

phrases.english: Let the "or"s of a murderer prove otherwise –
for they are "or"s,
and they speak about something that is not a monetary claim!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's comparison based on the shared word ״או״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: the רוצח passage has ״או״ but is not about money, so the word does not point to money.

steps.title: Compare only "or"s that come with an oath
steps.stepSummary: We compare ״או״ passages that involve an oath only to other ״או״ passages that involve an oath. The רוצח passage has no oath, so it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn "or"s that come with an oath from "or"s that come with an oath. The murderer's "or"s cannot prove anything, because there is no oath there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the comparison by making it narrower. It is not just the word "or", but "or" together with an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שבועת העדות and שבועת הפקדון share two features: the repeated ״או״ and an oath. The רוצח passage has only the first, so it is not similar enough to break the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learn" or "we compare": drawing a rule from a similar case
That have an oath with them

phrases.english: We learn "or"s that have an oath with them
from "or"s that have an oath with them,
and the "or"s of a murderer cannot prove otherwise –
since they have no oath with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין ״אוֹאִין״ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהֶן שְׁבוּעָה מֵ״אוֹאִין״ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהֶן שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רוצח challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the comparison by adding a second shared feature (an oath).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison rests only on the word ״או״, so any ״או״ passage could break it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison rests on ״או״ together with an oath, which the רוצח passage lacks.

steps.title: Challenge from the "or"s of סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The סוטה passage has repeated ״או״ and also an oath, yet it is not about money. So it seems to break the narrowed comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the "or"s of a סוטה prove otherwise! They are "or"s, they come with an oath, and they are not talking about money claims.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, this time using the new, narrower rule. It finds a passage with both features that is still not about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said ״או״ plus an oath points to money. The סוטה passage has ״או״ and an oath, since the כהן makes her swear, but it is about suspected unfaithfulness, not money. So even the narrowed comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife suspected of being unfaithful, who is made to swear by the כהן

phrases.english: Let the "or"s of a sota prove otherwise –
for they are "or"s, and they have an oath with them,
and they speak about something that is not a monetary claim!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed comparison from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that ״או״ plus an oath points to a money case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example that has both features (״או״ and an oath) but is not about money.

steps.title: Adding 'no כהן' to the comparison, which removes סוטה
steps.stepSummary: We compare only ״או״ passages that have an oath and no כהן. שבועת הפקדון fits this exactly. רוצח has no oath, and סוטה has a כהן, so neither one can disprove the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn ״או״ passages that have an oath and no כהן from ״או״ passages that have an oath and no כהן. The ״או״ words of רוצח cannot disprove this, because they have no oath. The ״או״ words of סוטה cannot disprove it either, because even though they have an oath, a כהן is involved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the סוטה challenge. It narrows the comparison once more: it now uses only ״או״ passages that have an oath AND no כהן running the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the rule was 'oath passages only', and that is why סוטה, which also has an oath, could challenge it. Now a second condition is added. In סוטה the כהן gives the oath, while in שבועת העדות and שבועת הפקדון no כהן is involved. That makes שבועת הפקדון, a money case, the closest match, so שבועת העדות is also limited to money.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or compare one case from another
The repeated words ״או״ ('or') in a parsha
Priest; in סוטה he is the one who gives the oath
And let them not disprove; this case cannot be used as a counter-proof
A woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful, who is given an oath by the כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The final form of רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה: ״או״ passages with an oath and no כהן (שבועת העדות) are learned from ״או״ passages with an oath and no כהן (שבועת הפקדון), so both deal only with money.

phrases.english: We infer ״or״s that have an oath with them
phrases.notes: This first set of ״or״s is in the parsha of שבועת העדות.

phrases.english: and have no priest with them,
from ״or״s that have an oath with them
phrases.notes: This second set is in the parsha of שבועת הפקדון, which deals with money.

phrases.english: and have no priest with them;
and the ״or״s of the murderer cannot disprove this –
since there is no oath with them;
and the ״or״s of the סוטה cannot disprove this –

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהֶן שְׁבוּעָה,
phrases.english: since even though there is an oath with them,
there is a priest with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין ״אוֹאִין״ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהֶן שְׁבוּעָה וְאֵין עִמָּהֶן כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סוטה challenge of step 15 by adding a second condition to the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the comparison by adding a distinguishing feature (no כהן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ״או״ passage with an oath counts, so סוטה, which is not about money, breaks the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ״או״ passages with an oath and no כהן count. סוטה has a כהן and is excluded, so the comparison to שבועת הפקדון stands.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the money limit from the word 'of these'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'מאלה' (of these) as limiting: only some cases bring liability. A witness asked to testify about money is liable, and about other matters he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these'. Some of these make him liable, and some of these leave him exempt. How so? If the person asked him to testify about money, he is liable. If it was about another matter, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different source for the rule from step 11 that שבועת העדות is only about money. He does not use a גזירה שוה. Instead he reads a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מאלה' means 'from among these', which suggests only part of a group. So רבי עקיבא splits testimony cases into two groups: money cases bring liability, and other matters do not. The proof rests on one word in the פסוק itself, not on comparing to another parsha.

keyTerms.meaning: Of these; a limiting word that means only some of the cases
Liable, here meaning he must bring a קרבן
Exempt
He demanded of him, the claimant asking the witness to testify
How so? A request to explain how the rule works

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
״And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these״ –
there are some of these for which he is liable,
and there are some of these for which he is exempt.
How so?
If he demanded his testimony about money – he is liable,
about another matter – he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהָיָה כִּי יֶאְשַׁם לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה has been fully defended, the ברייתא gives רבי עקיבא's separate source for the same rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that שבועת העדות applies only to money claims (step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting word 'מאלה' shows that only some cases bring liability, namely money cases.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'he saw or he knew'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the פסוק 'he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew' speaks about testimony that can rest on seeing without knowing, or on knowing without seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: The פסוק states 'and he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew'. The פסוק is speaking about testimony that holds up through seeing without knowing, and through knowing without seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives his own source for the money limit. He looks at the words 'saw' and 'knew' and says the פסוק describes a specific kind of testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'saw' and 'knew' as two separate ways a witness can know the facts: sight alone, or knowledge alone. The פסוק speaks only about testimony that can work either way. The ברייתא will now explain each way with an example, and those examples are money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeing; the witness saw the event himself
Knowing; the witness knows the facts without having seen the event
That is established or holds up
The פסוק is speaking about this case

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
The verse states
״And he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew״ –
about testimony that is established by sight without knowledge
and by knowledge without sight
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְהוּא עֵד אוֹ רָאָה אוֹ יָדָע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for the same rule, after רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that שבועת העדות applies only to money claims (step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'saw or knew' limit the פסוק to testimony that can rest on sight alone or on knowledge alone.

steps.title: What is 'seeing without knowing'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for an example of testimony based on sight without knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sight without knowledge: how does that work?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. The ברייתא now wants a concrete example of the first type of testimony that רבי יוסי הגלילי described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule is abstract. To understand which cases the פסוק covers, we need real-life examples of each type, and this question asks for the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: How? Asking for a practical example

phrases.english: Sight without knowledge – how so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the first category named in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case of testimony based on seeing without knowing.

steps.title: Example: 'I counted out a מנה for you in front of witnesses'
steps.stepSummary: The claimant says he counted out a מנה for the other person in front of two named people. The other person answers, 'Let them come and testify.' This is sight without knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: One person says: 'I counted out a מנה for you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so.' The other says: 'Let so-and-so and so-and-so come and testify.' This is sight without knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the example. It is a money case where the witnesses saw coins being counted out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses really did see the money being counted, so there is sight. But the case is called 'without knowledge', because seeing the coins counted does not tell them what the money was for. The example is a money claim, and that fits רבי יוסי הגלילי's point that the פסוק speaks about money testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
I counted out
So-and-so, a stand-in for a person's name
And they will testify

phrases.english: ״I counted out a maneh for you
in front of so-and-so and so-and-so״,
״Let so-and-so and so-and-so come and testify״ –
this is sight without knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 with a concrete money case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses who saw money counted out in a loan claim are an example of sight without knowledge.

steps.title: What is knowing without seeing?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for an example of testimony based on knowledge without sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can a witness know something without seeing it happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא already gave an example of 'seeing without knowing' (Step 20). Now it asks for the other kind, 'knowing without seeing,' and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי said the פסוק 'or he saw, or he knew' speaks about both kinds of testimony. To prove these kinds exist only in money cases, the ברייתא needs an example of each. This question asks for the second example.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing about something
Seeing something happen
How so? What is an example?

phrases.english: Knowledge without sight, how so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 19, now asking about the second kind of testimony.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where a witness knows the fact but never saw the event itself.

steps.title: The example: witnesses heard the admission
steps.stepSummary: The claimant says the other person admitted to owing a מנה in front of two people. The other person answers, 'Let them come and testify.' This is knowledge without sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: One person says: 'You admitted to me in front of so-and-so and so-and-so that you owe me a מנה.' The other says: 'Let them come and testify.' This is knowing without seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a case where the witnesses only heard the borrower admit the debt. They never saw the loan happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses know about the debt because they heard the admission, but they did not see any money handed over. So both kinds of testimony from רבי יוסי הגלילי are shown, and both are about money. This proves the פסוק is speaking about money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
You admitted
So-and-so and so-and-so (two named witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: 'seeing without knowing' and 'knowing without seeing' only happen in money cases, so שבועת העדות is only about money.

phrases.english: 'You admitted to me about a hundred dinars'
'in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,'
'Let so-and-so and so-and-so come and testify'
phrases.notes: This is what the other person answers. The witnesses heard him admit the debt, but they never saw the loan.

phrases.english: This is knowledge without sight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָנֶה הוֹדֵיתָה לִי בִּפְנֵי פְּלוֹנִי וּפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 and completes רבי יוסי הגלילי's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses who heard the debtor admit the debt know about it without having seen the loan.

steps.title: רבי שמעון compares the oath to the deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the תורה made one liable here and also with a פקדון. Just as פקדון is only about money claims, this oath is also only about money claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The תורה made a person liable here, and it made a person liable with a deposit. There it speaks only about money claims, so here too it speaks only about money claims.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא, רבי שמעון, gives a different proof that שבועת העדות is only about money. He compares it to שבועת הפקדון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both passages use the language of being 'liable' for a false oath. Since שבועת הפקדון is clearly about a money claim, רבי שמעון learns that שבועת העדות is also only about money claims.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the Torah) made liable
A deposit (an item left with someone for safekeeping)
There, in the other place
A claim about money

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
He made liable here, and He made liable with a deposit;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means שבועת העדות. 'He' is the תורה.

phrases.english: just as there it speaks
only about a money claim,
so too here it speaks
only about a money claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חִיֵּיב כָּאן וְחִיֵּיב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the ברייתא's question in step 11, after רבי אליעזר, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי, giving a different source for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: That שבועת העדות applies only to money claims.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to שבועת הפקדון, which is only about money.

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins a קל וחומר from פקדון
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון adds a second proof, a קל וחומר. With a פקדון, women are like men, relatives like non-relatives, and unfit people like fit ones, and one is liable for...
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, there is a קל וחומר: With a deposit, the תורה treated women like men, relatives like non-relatives, and unfit people like fit people, and a person is liable for...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון starts a second proof, a קל וחומר from פקדון. The amud ends in the middle of his sentence, and the argument finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He first points out how broad the deposit oath is: anyone can be liable, even women, relatives and unfit people. Witnesses for testimony are much more limited. He will use this difference to build the קל וחומר, which continues after 'liable for.'

keyTerms.meaning: A logical 'how much more so' argument
Relatives
People unfit to testify
People fit to testify

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not try to work out the conclusion yet, because it comes right after 'liable for.'

phrases.english: And furthermore, an a fortiori argument:
If with a deposit, where He made
women like men,
relatives like non-relatives,
unfit people like fit people;
phrases.notes: With a deposit, anyone can swear and be liable. For testimony, only fit witnesses count.

phrases.english: and he is liable for

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון adds a second proof alongside his comparison in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That שבועת העדות applies only to money claims.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the broad rules of שבועת הפקדון (it continues on the next amud).
